title: Cardinality / one-hot constraint sum x = k
text: Penalty (sum_i x_i - k)^2 = (1-2k) sum x_i + 2 sum_{i<j} x_i x_j + k^2. It couples every pair of variables in the constraint (dense), and its minimum violation is 1 (one item too many or too few). One-hot is the k = 1 case. Dense coupling means long chains on D-Wave as n grows.
source: Lucas, Ising formulations of many NP problems, Front. Phys. 2014

title: Pairwise exclusion x_i + x_j <= 1
text: Penalty x_i x_j: one quadratic term per forbidden pair, zero when at most one is chosen, minimum violation 1. Sparse and well-conditioned; violations usually mean the weight is below the value gained by taking both items.

title: Inequality with binary slack sum w x <= C
text: Turned into an equality with slack bits: (sum w_i x_i + sum c_b s_b - C)^2 with log-encoded slack. Coefficients grow with the square of the weights (w_i w_j, C w_i), so the coefficient dynamic range is large and grows with C. Extra slack variables enlarge the search space, and many states are 'feasible but slack wrong' with positive penalty. Feasibility should be judged on the original inequality, not the penalty.
source: Lucas 2014; Glover, Kochenberger and Du, A tutorial on formulating and using QUBO models (2019)

title: Unbalanced penalization (alternative to slack)
text: Encodes an inequality without slack variables using a linear plus quadratic penalty on h(x) = C - sum w x that is small for h >= 0 and large for h < 0. Avoids slack bits and reduces dynamic range, but the argmin is no longer guaranteed exact, so it is a formulation rewrite (high-risk action, must be re-verified).
source: Montanez-Barrera et al., Unbalanced penalization, arXiv:2211.13914

title: Domain-wall encoding of discrete variables
text: Encodes a variable with m values in m-1 qubits with a chain-like penalty instead of one-hot; fewer variables and sparser couplings, often better on annealing hardware. A formulation rewrite: must go back to the front end and be re-verified.
source: Chancellor, Domain wall encoding of discrete variables for quantum annealing and QAOA, Quantum Sci. Technol. 2019

title: Max-Cut (unconstrained)
text: Objective only: minimise sum_{ij} w_ij (2 x_i x_j - x_i - x_j). No penalties, so penalty actions do not apply; only sampling and solver parameters matter. Every bitstring is feasible.

title: Market Split (QOBLIB class 01): equality system A x = b
text: Feasibility problem: QUBO = sum_i (b_i - a_i.x)^2, one squared penalty per row; objective value 0 means a feasible solution. Coefficients grow with a_ij * b_i (e.g. |q| up to 56,477 with dynamic range ~84 for m=3, n=20, a_ij <= 50), so precision is tight. Known to be very hard for every solver class. Measured with SA: default (100 reads x 1000 sweeps) found 0 feasible samples at n=20; 1000 reads x 20000 sweeps found about 1 in 1000; re-weighting rows (1:2:4) did not help. Success is binary per run (feasible found or not), so more independent reads/restarts matter more than penalty balancing; when the budget is small, expect failure.
source: QOBLIB (Koch et al., arXiv:2504.03832; data CC BY 4.0) + our SA measurements 2026-10-04

title: Maximum Independent Set (QOBLIB class 07)
text: QUBO: maximise sum_v x_v - P * sum_(u,v) in E x_u x_v; QOBLIB uses P = 2. The single-flip floor is 1, so P must be strictly greater than 1 (P = 1 ties feasible and infeasible states). Sparse graphs embed on D-Wave with short chains. Measured: SA defaults found the proven optimum on every tested QOBLIB graph up to 200 nodes (karate, football, hamming6-4, johnson8-4-4, C125-9, brock200-1, keller4). None of QOBLIB's 2,377 submissions for classes 01/02/03/07 used an annealer; quantum-hardware entries are gate-based (mostly QAOA).
source: QOBLIB (Koch et al., arXiv:2504.03832; data CC BY 4.0) + our SA measurements 2026-10-04
